ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Iowa City set with soaring solos and flawless China → Rider
ai_show_review.blurb: The August 10, 1982 Fieldhouse show delivers nonstop momentum, highlighted by a blistering China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue and an inspired Lost Sailor → Saint Of Circumstance → Eyes Of The World suite. Jerry’s leads are on fire throughout, while Brent adds tight vocal harmonies and the rhythm section drives a powerful second‑set arc. Multiple soundboard and matrix sources capture the performance with crystal clarity.
ai_show_review.review:
What unfolds at the Fieldhouse is a textbook example of early‑’80s Dead in top form. The first set builds steady excitement, kicking off with a punchy Feel Like A Stranger and moving through classics like Cassidy and It Must Have Been The Roses before launching into a thunderous Bertha that sets the tone for the night. The second set is where the magic really clicks – China Cat Sunflower flows seamlessly into I Know You Rider, then the band dives deep into a Lost Sailor → Saint Of Circumstance → Eyes Of The World marathon that showcases Jerry’s lyrical yet incendiary leads and Phil’s thumping bass foundation. After a tight Drums‑Space pair, the group rides a high‑octane wave through Iko Iko, Truckin', Stella Blue, and finishes with an exuberant Sugar Magnolia before a double encore of folk‑rock standards. Across all available recordings the mix is superb; Miller soundboards give pristine separation while the matrix blends add ambient depth, making this one of the most listenable August ’82 shows.

Every musician shines: Jerry’s solos are both breakneck and melodic, especially on Eyes Of The World and his feel‑good lead on Feel Like A Stranger. Phil’s bass is solid and occasionally bombastic, anchoring the improvisations even when his signal sits low in the mix. Bob’s gritty vocal on Iko Iko adds character, while Brent’s keyboards provide rich organ textures and his backing vocals blend beautifully with the harmonies. Mickey’s snare work propels the jams, and Bill’s drumming locks in with Hart for a driving rhythmic backbone that never lets the energy dip.

best_recording.reason: Miller soundboard with crystal‑clear mix, excellent channel separation and only a brief distortion hiccup, capturing the full dynamics of the performance.

key_highlights: Flawless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition that launches the second set.
Lost Sailor → Saint Of Circumstance → Eyes Of The World suite delivering sustained high energy.
Jerry’s soaring leads on Eyes Of The World and Feel Like A Stranger, plus a standout vocal moment on Iko Iko.
Exceptional recording quality across multiple sources; Miller SBD is the clearest reference.
song_highlights: It Must Have Been The Roses

band_performance.Jerry: Soaring, lyrical leads throughout; especially incendiary solos on Eyes Of The World and a crisp, expressive lead on Feel Like A Stranger.
band_performance.Phil: Solid, thumping bass that underpins the high‑energy jams; occasional low mix level but still drives Lost Sailor → Saint → Eyes suite with authority.
band_performance.Bob: Raspy vocal delivery shines on Iko Iko and adds gritty rhythm guitar texture across the set.
band_performance.Brent: Rich B3 organ and electric piano textures, strong backing vocals that enhance harmonies, especially during the second‑set transitions.
band_performance.Mickey: Snappy snare work that fuels Jerry’s leads; drum mix praised for separation and punch.
band_performance.Billy: Steady, propulsive drumming that locks in with Mickey, providing a solid rhythmic foundation throughout.
